memory_leads.lead: Crewing is a chain of distinct roles rather than one employer relationship: owner/operator, crew manager, manning or recruitment intermediary, master and department heads, individual seafarer, training/medical/certification functions, payroll/travel support and authority interfaces can all participate in putting one person aboard.

Required manning and actual onboard complement are separate states. A vessel can have a planned or required rank structure while a vacancy, relief delay or document problem makes the actual available complement different; exact safe-manning scales remain source-specific.

Recruitment begins with vacancy and candidate-pool states: sourcing, application, identity/experience review, references or prior-service checks, interview or technical screening and selection can precede formal document readiness and employment.

Seafarer readiness is multidimensional. Rank or competency certification, flag or other endorsements where applicable, medical fitness documentation, mandatory or company training, passport/visa and travel documents can expire or become ready on different clocks; one valid document does not imply complete readiness.

Employment acceptance, contract or articles signing and actual service commencement are separate transitions. A selected and contracted seafarer may still be ashore awaiting travel, while an onboard seafarer's planned contract end may precede actual relief and disembarkation.

Crew-change logistics form a travel-and-clearance state machine: visa/entry readiness, flights or ground transport, hotel or waiting arrangements, port-agent coordination, launch/terminal access, immigration or other formalities and vessel arrival must align for embarkation or relief.

Embarkation is not instantly equivalent to effective watchkeeping or departmental handover. Joining, familiarization, rank assignment, transfer of duties and the relieved person's sign-off/disembarkation can overlap, making crew-change time a bounded transition rather than a single timestamp.

Rotation and relief planning create a forward queue. Planned relief date, replacement nomination, document readiness, travel booking, vessel-port opportunity and actual relief may diverge; repeated extension can affect fatigue, morale, retention and future staffing without proving a particular legal violation.

Payroll and seafarer administration have their own durable states: wage entitlement periods, payroll calculation, allotments/remittances, deductions or adjustments, leave balances and payment confirmation can differ from physical onboard service dates, while exact terms are agreement-specific.

Work/rest, fatigue and welfare should be treated as evolving operational conditions rather than a binary fit/unfit flag. Watch patterns, port intensity, maintenance workload, extended tours, communications access and living conditions can affect human performance, but exact records and fitness conclusions require Evidence.

Training readiness can continue after initial certification through vessel familiarization, equipment- or cargo-specific instruction, drills, promotion preparation and recurrent company training. Completion, demonstrated competence and later operational performance should not be collapsed into one state.

Illness, injury or other inability to continue service can trigger medical assessment, temporary onboard limitation, shore treatment, disembarkation, replacement sourcing and repatriation on different clocks. The existence of this workflow does not establish a person's diagnosis or legal entitlement.

Retention and crew continuity create a fleet-level capability state. Turnover, promotion pipelines, repeated return to the same vessel or fleet and availability of experienced senior officers can influence operating consistency and training burden without justifying nationality, agency or individual quality rankings.

P058 management governance is refined because delegating crew management does not itself create onboard readiness: candidate, document, employment, travel, relief and retention queues must actually resolve before the delegated mandate becomes usable crew capacity.

P052 port-call memory is refined because crew changes are another port-call dependency: vessel ETA, agent coordination, immigration/access and joining/leaving travel can constrain each other even when cargo and berth operations are otherwise ready.

P057 technical-management memory is refined because maintenance and defect closure depend on onboard engineering capacity, familiarization, workload and specialist competence as well as parts and shore service availability.

P054 casualty memory is refined because master/crew availability, fatigue, familiarization and relief timing belong to the contemporaneous operating context, while they must not be backfilled as causal fault merely because a later investigation discusses human factors.

P058 already distinguishes crew manager, master and onboard crew as separate roles. P059 adds the individual seafarer readiness/rotation/employment lifecycle rather than rediscovering the governance distinction.
P052 already includes immigration, husbandry and crew-logistics interfaces during port calls. P059 reuses that handoff for embarkation and relief rather than creating a second port-agency process.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Manning and personal qualification requirements vary by vessel, flag, trade, rank and rule vintage and require authoritative Evidence.
Employment and labor terms are agreement- and jurisdiction-specific source facts.
Personal records and fitness/performance conclusions require protected claim-scoped Evidence and should not be inferred from structural Memory.
Provider identity, current capability and demographic quality claims are source-first questions outside blind Memory.

stop_reason: The seafarer lifecycle is populated from manning need and recruitment through multidimensional document/training readiness, employment, travel/embarkation, handover, rotation/relief, payroll, fatigue/welfare, medical/repatriation and retention. Further recall becomes wage-, contract-, certificate-, manning-scale-, personal-record-, provider-, union- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation and not employment, labor, medical, crewing, safety, immigration or legal advice; no safe-manning requirement, certificate, medical status, employment term, wage, payroll item, visa, fatigue record, training competence, individual fitness, provider capability or labor-law conclusion is verified.
